description: Replaces or shifts the octave of a V/Oct signal at random, with a fader per octave setting how often each one is chosen and a seed that makes the pattern repeatable

params.text: Sets how often this octave is chosen; at zero it is never used, and the faders are weighed against each other rather than adding up to anything
Adds up to a hundred cents of random detuning to each note
Returns the internal seed to its stored value, so the same pattern of octaves plays again
Draws a new internal seed from the clock, giving a fresh pattern of octaves

inputs.text: The pitch to be re-octaved; each polyphonic channel is treated on its own
Marks where one note ends and the next begins, so a new octave can be drawn; each polyphonic channel is treated on its own
Returns the internal seed to its stored value when the voltage rises past 2V
Draws a new internal seed when the voltage rises past 2V

outputs.text: The re-octaved pitch, with as many channels as the wider of the two inputs
The gate input passed through, with as many channels as the wider of the two inputs

notes: with nothing patched into the gate input the octave is redrawn whenever the incoming pitch changes
the fader row is read differently in each mode, so the number under a fader means an absolute octave, a shift in octaves, or an interval, depending on what the menu is set to
in Absolute the ten faders are the octaves 0 to 9, and the one chosen replaces the octave of the incoming note
in Relative the ten faders are shifts of minus five to plus five octaves, added to the octave of the incoming note
in Relative + Intervals the top row of faders is shifts of minus two to plus three octaves and the bottom row is intervals set below the note
menu: Mode: Absolute, Relative, Relative + Intervals — chooses how the row of faders is read, and swaps the panel artwork to match

inputs.2:
unipolar · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
